name: Southern Russia & the Caucasus (Krasnodar · Rostov · Dagestan · Sochi)

language.script_notes: In the North Caucasus republics (Dagestan, Chechnya, Ingushetia) local titular languages and Arabic religious script also appear on signs and buildings.

road_furniture.guardrail_type: Steel W-beam; mountain roads in the Caucasus have long exposed drops.
road_furniture.line_paint: White lines on the M4 'Don' highway and main routes; many steppe and mountain roads unmarked.
road_furniture.km_marker_style: White sign poles with a black base band. The M4 corridor carries heavy holiday traffic toward the Black Sea.

architecture.roof_style: Low-pitched and flat roofs on single-storey steppe houses; ornate multi-storey houses and minarets in the Caucasus.
architecture.roof_material: Sheet metal, tile, some flat concrete.
architecture.wall_construction: Brick and rendered single-storey houses across the Kuban and Don steppe, often with a walled yard; taller, more decorated brick houses in the North Caucasus; resort blocks around Sochi.
architecture.wall_color_palette: Whitewash, brick, and pastel render; brighter and more ornamented than central Russia.
architecture.distinctive_building_types: Cossack-style steppe farmhouses with courtyards; mosques with minarets in the Muslim-majority republics (a strong 'this is the south' tell); Sochi's subtropical resort architecture and palm-lined promenades.

nature.vegetation: Wheat and huge yellow sunflower fields across the Kuban and Don steppe — the sunflowers are a strong southern signal — plus vineyards and orchards. Subtropical growth (palms, tea, magnolia, cypress) on the Black Sea coast around Sochi.
nature.terrain: Flat to gently rolling steppe in the north; the wall of the Greater Caucasus (up to Elbrus, 5,600 m) along the south; a narrow, steep Black Sea coastal strip.
nature.climate_signature: The warmest part of Russia — hot dry steppe summers, mild low-snow winters, and humid subtropical conditions at Sochi. Much less snow in the coverage than anywhere else in the country.

vehicles.plate_color: White with a region number — codes in the 20s, 60s, 90s and 160s cover Krasnodar, Rostov, Stavropol and the Caucasus republics.
vehicles.distinctive_vehicles: National mix, left-hand drive. Agricultural machinery and grain trucks on the steppe.

google_coverage.coverage_notes: Good coverage along the M4 corridor, the Kuban and the Black Sea coast; patchier in the mountain republics. Scenes are sunnier and greener than the Russian norm.

confusion_set.shared_traits: The wheat-and-sunflower steppe runs straight across the border; Cyrillic; similar villages
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Ukrainian plates have a blue EU-style strip and Ukrainian spelling; Russian plates carry a region number.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Same country — Cyrillic, panelki, Russian plates
confusion_set.tiebreaker: The south is warm and low-snow with sunflower fields, minarets and (near Sochi) palms; central Russia is birch forest, snow and onion domes.

confusion_set.shared_traits: The Greater Caucasus mountains, similar terrain and vegetation on the southern slopes
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Georgian uses its own rounded script and Georgian/Latin plates; Russian side is Cyrillic with region-number plates.
